title: Improved Friedgut threshold
statement: Let $n,k\in\mathbb N$, let $f$ be a Boolean function on $\{−1,1\}^n$ with values in $\{−1,1\}$, and let $\epsilon,\eta\in\mathbb R$. Its improved Friedgut threshold is $\left(\frac{\epsilon}{I(f)}\rho(\eta)^k\right)^{1+\eta}$, where $I(f)$ is the total influence of $f$ and $\rho(\eta)=\frac{\eta}{2+\eta}$.
hypotheses_covered: Boolean function $f$ on $\{−1,1\}^n$ with values in $\{−1,1\}$
